11.sol: Xylem is the main conducting tissue in plants. It consists of 4 different components - tracheids, trachea or vessels, xylem fibre and xylem parenchyma. Tracheids are elongated cells with tapering end. They are generally present in ferns and gymnosperms for conduction of water. In angiosperms, vessels are composite structure as these are formed by dissolution of end walls of row of cells i.e., vessels elements. 105.text: Which of the following is a predatory fungus?
105.sol: Arthrobotrys is a genus of mitosporic fungi in the Family Orbiliaceae. It is a predatory fungus that captures and feeds on nematode worms. Rings that form on the fungal hyphae constrict and entrap worms, then hyphae grow into the worm and digest it.

2015.sol: Based on the mode of secretion, the glands are of three types : mesocrine, apocrine and holocrine. Mammary glands that are present in mammals to feed the young ones with milk are the example of apocrine glands. In apocrine glands, the secretion accumulates as secretory granules in the distal part of the cell. This part later breaks down and leaves as a secretion.

2079.sol: One of the hormones released by the placenta is human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG). This hormone is secreted by the trophoblast cells even before they become the chorion, and is the hormone assayed in the pregnancy test. Because its action is almost identical to that of luteinizing hormone (LH), hCG maintains the mother's corpus luteum. 20484.sol: Boron trihalides are Lewis acids. The back bonding determines its acidic strength, more is the -back bonding, less is the acidity. 55112.text: What is the product formed on Rosenmund reduction of benzoyl chloride ?
55112.sol: Rosenmund reduction is the catalytic hydrogenation of an acid chloride to an aldehyde. The reagent used is hydrogen gas in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulfate ( H₂ / Pd-BaSO₄ ). When benzoyl chloride ( C₆H₅COCl ) is subjected to Rosenmund reduction, it is reduced to benzaldehyde ( C₆H₅CHO ). The reaction is: C₆H₅COCl + H₂ Pd/BaSO₄ C₆H₅CHO + HCl Therefore, the product formed is benzaldehyde. Answer: Benzaldehyde

55451.subject: Chemistry
55451.text: Which of the following compounds forms starch on polymerization?
55451.sol: Starch is a polysaccharide composed of two components: amylose and amylopectin. Both amylose and amylopectin are polymers of -D-glucose. Amylose is a linear polymer with C1-C4 glycosidic linkages, while amylopectin is a branched polymer with C1-C4 and C1-C6 glycosidic linkages. Therefore, starch is formed by the polymerization of -D-glucose. Answer: -D-glucose.

71641.sol: The structure of tert-butyl amine is (CH₃)₃C-NH₂ . The degree of an amine is determined by the number of alkyl or aryl groups directly attached to the nitrogen atom. 84015.sol: Organic forming is the form of agriculture that relies on techniques such as crop rotation, green manure, compost and biological pest control to maintain soil productivity. It excludes the use of manufactured fertilizers, pesticides, plant growth regulators, genetically modified organisms, live stock antibiotics, etc. It uses only naturally produced inputs like composts.

84061.subject: Zoology
84061.text: All the components of the nodal tissue are autoexcitable. Why does the SA node act as the normal pacemaker?
options: SA node has the lowest rate of depolarisation
SA node is the only component to generate the threshold potential
Only SA node can convey the action potential to the other components
SA node has the highest rate of depolarisation
84061.sol: The nodal musculature has the ability to generate action potentials without any external stimuli, i.e. it is autoexcitable. However, the number of action potentials that could be generated in a minute vary at different parts of the nodal system. The SAN (Sino-Atrial Node) can generate the maximum number of action potentials, i.e 70-75 ~min , i.e. the highest rate of depolarisation and is responsible for initiating and maintaining the rhythmic contractile activity of the heart. Therefore, it is called pacemaker.

Adipose tissues are loose connective tissues that are made up of fat cells called adipose cells or adipocytes.

108626.sol: Expansion into an evacuated vessel (vacuum) is called free expansion. In this case, the external pressure ( P_ ext ) is zero. Work done, w = -P_ ext V = 0 . Since the process is isothermal and involves an ideal gas, the change in temperature ( T ) is zero. The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, so U = 0 . 128846.subject: Zoology
128846.text: What type of circulation do fishes have?
128846.sol: : All vertebrates possess a muscular chambered heart. Fishes have a 2-chambered heart with an atrium and a ventricle. Amphibians and the reptiles (except crocodiles) have a 3-chambered heart with two atria and a single ventricle, whereas crocodiles, birds and mammals possess a 4-chambered heart with two atria and two ventricles . In fishes the heart pumps out deoxygenated blood which is oxygenated by the gills and supplied to the body parts from where deoxygenated blood is returned to the heart (single circulation)

131457.text: What was the main goal of Hershey and Chase's experiments?
options: To determine whether protein or DNA entered the bacteria from viruses
To prove that RNA is the genetic material
To isolate the transforming principle in bacteriophages
To determine the chemical composition of bacteriophages
131457.sol: The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952). They worked with viruses that infect bacteria called bacteriophages. The bacteriophage attaches to the bacteria and its genetic material then enters the bacterial cell. The bacterial cell treats the viral genetic material as if it was its own and subsequently manufactures more virus particles . The DNA sequence coding for tRNA or rRNA molecules also defines a gene. However by defining a cistron as a segment of DNA coding for a polypeptide, the structural gene in a transcription unit could be said as monocistronic (mostly in eukaryotes) or polycistronic (mostly in bacteria or prokaryotes). 132860.subject: Zoology
132860.text: Human ancestors Timeline of origin A. Australopithecines 1. 75,000-10,000 years ago B. Homo erectus 2. 1,00,000-40,000 years back C. Neanderthal man 3. about 1.5 mya D. Homo sapiens 4. 2 mya
132860.sol: Australopithecines existed around 2 million years ago (mya), marking early hominin evolution. Homo erectus emerged about 1.5 mya, known for significant advances in tool use and migration. Neanderthal man lived between 1,00,000-40,000 years ago, known for their adaptation to cold climates and complex tools. Homo sapiens appeared around 75,000-10,000 years ago, representing modern humans who developed advanced culture and technology.

132898.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because the placental wolf (a placental mammal) and the Tasmanian wolf (a marsupial) evolved independently from different lineages but developed similar phenotypic features due to adapting to similar ecological niches, which is a classic example of convergent evolution. Reason (R) is incorrect because the process where a single ancestral species evolves into different forms to occupy different habitats is the definition of adaptive radiation (which leads to divergent evolution). 134457.subject: Zoology
134457.text: What is the result of cutting DNA by restriction endonucleases?
134457.sol: Restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the center of the palindrome sites, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands. This leaves single stranded portions at the ends. There are overhanging stretches called sticky ends on each strand. These are named so because they form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts. This stickiness of the ends facilitates the action of the enzyme DNA ligase.

135379.text: A laboratory experiment is conducted where a yeast culture is grown in a test tube containing a fixed, limited concentration of sugar. When the population size is plotted against time, the curve shows an initial slow increase, followed by a rapid phase, and eventually flattens out at a maximum of 500 cells. Which mathematical model best describes this growth pattern, and what ecological term corresponds to the value

Logistic growth model and Intrinsic rate of natural increase
Logistic growth model and Carrying capacity
Geometric growth model and Environmental resistance
135379.sol: The yeast culture is grown in a medium with a fixed, limited concentration of sugar, which means resources are finite. When resources are finite, population growth eventually slows down and stops as it reaches the maximum number of individuals the environment can support. This pattern—an initial lag phase, followed by a phase of acceleration and deceleration, and finally an asymptote—is characteristic of the Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth model. 6a13e46a688ac6d0667aad8f.text: Consider the following sexually transmitted infections: I. Syphilis II. Genital herpes III. Chlamydiasis IV. Hepatitis-B V. Gonorrhoea Which of the infections listed above are NOT completely curable even if detected early and treated properly?
6a13e46a688ac6d0667aad8f.sol: According to the NCERT Biology curriculum on Reproductive Health, sexually transmitted infections (STIs) such as syphilis, gonorrhoea, chlamydiasis, and trichomoniasis are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. However, viral infections like hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV are exceptions. These infections are not completely curable even if detected early. From the given list, Genital herpes (II) and Hepatitis-B (IV) are the infections that are not completely curable. Answer: II and IV

6a1bb6bf107bf677676d9f89.sol: Conservation strategies are broadly classified into in situ (on-site) and ex situ (off-site) conservation. Ex situ conservation involves protecting endangered species of plants and animals outside their natural habitats. Examples include botanical gardens, zoological parks, wildlife safari parks, seed banks, and cryopreservation techniques. In situ conservation involves protecting species in their natural habitats. Examples include national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, and sacred groves. From th

6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9f9a.subject: Biology
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9f9a.text: Earthworms feed on fragmented plant remains and soil organic matter in an agricultural field. Ecologically, they are participating in which of the following pathways of energy flow?
options: Grazing food chain as primary producers
Parasitic food chain as primary consumers
Grazing food chain as secondary consumers
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9f9a.sol: Earthworms feed on dead and decaying organic matter, such as fragmented plant remains and soil organic matter, which is known as detritus. Organisms that feed on detritus are called detritivores. By breaking down this organic matter, they play a crucial role in the detritus food chain, facilitating the recycling of nutrients back into the ecosystem. Therefore, earthworms participate in the detritus food chain as detritivores. Answer: Detritus food chain as detritivores

95310.subject: Botany
95310.text: The chief water-conducting elements of xylem in Sequoia tree are
95310.sol: The chief water-conducting element of xylem in gymnosperms are called tracheids. These are elongated cells with tapering ends and are dead because of the deposition of lignin. These show scalariform, annular, reticulate, or bordered pitted thickening. These are the only water-conducting xylem elements in both gymnosperms and pteridophytes. Generally, vessels are absent in gymnosperms with exceptions like Gnetum, Welwitschia , Ephedra , etc.

95539.subject: Botany
95539.text: Which of the following incorrect about Ichthyophis?
95539.sol: Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian. It belongs to the Order Apoda. External fertilization, oviparous nature and absence of exoskeleton are its features.

95957.subject: Botany
95957.text: If a subcellular fraction from liver tissue exhibits a high level of acid lipases, proteases, carbohydrases activity. The organelle associated with it will be
95957.sol: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.

96329.subject: Botany
96329.sol: During prophase, the nucleolus and nuclear membrane disappear and spindle grows between the centrosomes. The chromosomes get arranged at the equator of the cell during metaphase by the formation of spindle poles oppositely. Centromere splits, sister chromatids are broken down and chromatids are separated during anaphase and daughter chromosomes start moving towards the opposite poles. Nuclear membrane, nucleolus and ER reappears during telophase, thus two nuclei are formed.

97189.subject: Botany
97189.text: Which one of the following is a set of natural growth regulators?
97189.sol: Plant growth regulators are growth promoter and growth inhibitors. Those which are naturally synthesized by plants are natural growth regulators. Certain chemical substance when applied to plants shows similar effect and are reffered as synthetic hormone.

97466.subject: Botany
97466.text: Which of the following does not have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal?
97466.sol: The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. The capsule contains spores. Spores are formed after meiosis. The mosses have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal. Common examples of mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum, and Sphagnum. Riccia is a member of liverworts.

97578.subject: Botany
97578.text: In the electron transport system present in the inner mitochondrial membrane, complexes I and IV are respectively
options: NADH dehydrogenase and cytochrome-c oxidase complex
97578.sol: Complex I of the electron transport system (ETS) is NADH dehydrogenase, which oxidizes NADH produced in the mitochondrial matrix during the citric acid cycle. Cytochrome c oxidase or complex IV catalyzes the final step in the mitochondrial electron transfer chain and is regarded as one of the major regulation sites for oxidative phosphorylation.

97746.subject: Botany
97746.text: What is correct about the electron transport system?
options: Energy stored in ATPs is utilised for synthesis of NADH + H + .
Energy stored in ATPs is utilised for synthesis of F A D H 2 .
Energy stored in NADH + H + . and F A D H 2 is utilized for synthesis of ATPs.
Energy stored in glucose is utilized for synthesis of NADH + H + , and F A D H 2 only.
97746.sol: Mechanism of ATP production: When the electrons pass from one electron carrier to another carrier (from complex I to IV) in ETS, they are coupled to ATP synthase (complex V) and thus ATP are synthesized.

305172.text: A parallel-plate capacitor with a capacitance of 5 F is connected to a battery having an emf of 6 V . The separation between the plates is 2 mm . 306516.text: For a particular sample of an ideal gas, its energy depends solely on its
306516.sol: For an ideal gas, there are no intermolecular forces of attraction. Hence, the potential energy of the gas molecules is zero. The internal energy of an ideal gas consists entirely of kinetic energy, which is directly proportional to its absolute temperature. The internal energy is given by U = f 2 n R T , where f is the degree of freedom, n is the number of moles, R is the universal gas constant, and T is the absolute temperature. 6a7a1ff83677078afd8ceb42.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff83677078afd8ceb42.text: A block of mass m is released from rest on a rough inclined plane that makes an angle with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is . What is the kinetic energy of the block after it has slid a distance d down the plane?
6a7a1ff83677078afd8ceb42.sol: The forces doing work on the block as it slides down the incline are gravity and kinetic friction. The component of the gravitational force along the incline is mg . The work done by gravity over a distance d is W_g = mgd . The normal force on the block is N = mg . The kinetic friction force opposes the motion and has a magnitude f_k = N = mg . The work done by friction is W_f = -f_k d = - mgd . According to the work-energy theorem, the total work done on the block equals its change in kinetic energy. K = W_g + W_f
